color.text.code.accent.1: Use for an additional syntax-highlighting text color.
color.text.code.accent.2: Use for an additional syntax-highlighting text color.
color.text.code.comments: Use for comments in syntax-highlighted code.
color.text.code.default: Use for default text in code blocks and code diffs.
color.text.code.functions: Use for functions in syntax-highlighted code.
color.text.code.gutter: Use for line numbers and other code gutter text.
color.text.code.keywords: Use for language keywords in syntax-highlighted code.
color.text.code.numbers: Use for numeric values in syntax-highlighted code.
color.text.code.operators: Use for operators and punctuation in syntax-highlighted code.
color.text.code.strings: Use for string values in syntax-highlighted code.
color.text.code.tags: Use for tags in syntax-highlighted code.
color.text.disabled: Use for text in a disabled state.
color.text.inverse: Use for text on bold backgrounds.
color.text.selected: Use for text that communicates selection, such as the active tab or a selected navigation item, or the opened state of a dropdown trigger. On bold selected backgrounds, use color.text.inverse instead. Do not use for unselected links, brand emphasis, or hover alone. Keep the selected text treatment when the element also has focus.
color.text.brand: Use for text that reinforces our brand.
color.text.danger: Use for critical text, such as input field error messaging.
color.text.danger.bolder: Use for text on top of danger semantic labels to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.text.warning: Use for text to emphasize caution, such as in moved lozenges.
color.text.warning.inverse: Use for text when on bold warning backgrounds.
color.text.warning.bolder: Use for text on top of warning semantic labels to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.text.success: Use for text to communicate a favorable outcome, such as input field success messaging.
color.text.success.bolder: Use for text on top of success semantic labels to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.text.discovery: Use for text to emphasize change or something new, such as in new lozenges.
color.text.discovery.bolder: Use for text on top of discovery semantic labels to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.text.information: Use for informative text or to communicate something is in progress, such as in-progress lozenges.
color.text.information.bolder: Use for text on top of information semantic labels to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.text.subtlest: Use for tertiary text, such as meta-data, breadcrumbs, input field placeholder and helper text.
color.text.subtle: Use for secondary text, such as navigation, subtle button links, input field labels, and all caps subheadings.
color.icon: Use for icon-only buttons, or icons paired with color.text
